description:
## Problem
There is no specification ETL in BenchBox. The first part is reading DIGen's Batch 1 files into staging tables and loading the reference tables, including the XML and fixed-width files.

## Owner decisions (choice dialogs, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- 2026-11-21: "Make a new plan to base our TPC-DI implementation on it [shannon-barrow/databricks-tpc-di]. We will be using the DuckDB implementation for comparison. We MUST adhere as closely as possible to the spec/paper. We will be generalize and 'benchbox-ifying' the source to make it well integrated with BenchBox and consistent across platforms."
- 2026-11-21: "You will consider the license to be MIT for the purposes of this effort and we will include the usual TPC caveats and limitations."
- 2026-11-21: where the project and the specification differ, "The specification wins without asking. Every difference, and any behaviour of the project that is kept, goes in a catalogue I approve at the milestone stop. A difference from the DuckDB implementation not in the catalogue is a finding that blocks the step."
- 2026-11-21, XML on DuckDB: "require the existing 'allow third-party extensions' setting; refuse with a clear message without it. Never enable it silently." Message: "TPC-DI on DuckDB reads CustomerMgmt.xml with the community extension \"webbed\". Allow third-party extensions ({setting}) to continue."
- 2026-11-21, optimisations of the project that are specific to Databricks: "Optional tuning, off by default; the base SQL is the same on every platform."
- 2026-11-20: third-party engine extensions are allowed for XML.

## Change
First move the old Python package `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/` (14 modules, unreachable since the quarantine) to `benchbox/core/tpcdi/_legacy_etl/`, updating its internal imports, so the two never share a directory (owner, 2026-11-21). Then create `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/` with `LICENSE-databricks-tpc-di.txt` (package data), `PROVENANCE.json` (each SQL file: source path in the project at 8e0f944, kind adapted or rewritten, path in the DuckDB implementation where it was consulted), `DEPARTURES.yaml` and `ingest/*.sql`. The canonical dialect is DuckDB. Derive the SQL from the project's `src/incremental_batches/bronze/{CustomerMgmtRaw,ingest_finwire,raw_ingestion,Ingest_Incremental}` and `silver/DimBroker.sql`: translate Spark to DuckDB, remove every comment, replace notebook parameters with BenchBox parameters, and read Batch 1 only. Add `strategies.py` with the four per-platform choices (file ingestion, XML parsing, how history-tracked rows are applied, flag storage) and their DuckDB implementations; register choices through `sql_compat`, and record them for the result. XML: the community extension `webbed`, only when third-party extensions are allowed, with the owner's refusal message otherwise. Load DimDate, DimTime, Industry, StatusType, TaxRate, TradeType and DimBroker. Freeze the rendered DuckDB SQL in a new golden-corpus area. No per-platform SQL files. Staging reads use DECIMAL, not DOUBLE.

## Decision gates
Early check first: count the actions in `CustomerMgmt.xml` with `webbed` and with Python's incremental XML parser at scales 3, 5 and 10. If `webbed` returns fewer, do not split or rewrite the staging file: any split happens in a scratch directory inside the timed phase, and that fallback is described in the pull request before arming. The name of the existing setting that allows third-party extensions is read from `platforms/duckdb.py` and used in the message. Any Databricks-specific optimisation in the source files is left out and listed in `DEPARTURES.yaml`.

## Verification rubric
Pass: for every Batch 1 source file at scales 3 and 5, staging row counts equal DIGen's own row-count attributes in its audit files (a test over real output, run through `make heavy-run`, results in the pull request); the XML action count equals the Python parser's count; with third-party extensions not allowed the run refuses with the owner's exact message (test); a test asserts every `etl/**/*.sql` is in `PROVENANCE.json` and contains no comment; the golden renders are frozen; the provenance guard passes; no staging manifest changes; the CLI still refuses TPC-DI; `make comment-policy-check`, `make compat-inventory-check` and `make pr-preflight` pass. The built wheel lists `LICENSE-databricks-tpc-di.txt` and the SQL files (`unzip -l`); an import smoke test shows `_legacy_etl` still imports and nothing reaches it.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`.
- Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking. `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job the runner never ran or cancelled, never for a failed test.
- Review threads: reply; resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again.
- Subagents are read-only. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment.
- Any limit, default, threshold, status token, message, label text or name (option, configuration key, result field, file name, test hook) the owner has not already chosen is chosen by the implementer following existing BenchBox conventions and the specification, and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). Texts the owner has chosen (see tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120) are used verbatim.
- A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`. Delivery follows the batch plan on tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120: a batch member ends at a landing report and its batch has one final pull request; a serial item has its own pull request.
- From the quarantine step until the reopening step, no TPC-DI entry point may produce a result that reads PASSED or is admitted for publication.
- Sources. SQL derived from the Databricks project (`src/incremental_batches/**` at commit 8e0f944, treated as MIT on the owner's instruction) may be committed only after the provenance step has merged, only under `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/`, with every file listed in `PROVENANCE.json` and with all comments removed.
- TPC and bankmark files (DIGen, PDGF, dictionaries, configuration, EULA, appendix SQL) come only from the official archive the owner supplies, are committed unmodified and only in `_sources/tpc-di/`, `benchbox/_binaries/tpc-di/` and `benchbox/_binaries/tpc-di/tools/`. Never copy from the Databricks project or the DuckDB implementation: their copies of the tools or the tools zip, DIGen output, generated reference files, audit snapshots, their copy or rewrite of the appendix SQL, or any generator code (`src/tools/**`). Never commit DIGen output.
- The specification wins over the Databricks project without asking. Each behaviour of the project that is kept and each change made to follow the specification is one row in `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/DEPARTURES.yaml`, which the owner approves at the milestone stop.
- Owner, 2026-11-21: "The specification wins without asking. Every difference, and any behaviour of the project that is kept, goes in a catalogue I approve at the milestone stop. A difference from the DuckDB implementation not in the catalogue is a finding that blocks the step." The catalogue is `DEPARTURES.yaml`; every entry of the comparison's expected-differences list must cite a catalogue row. After the milestone stop, a new catalogue row in which BenchBox follows the specification is listed in the pull request; a row that would keep behaviour of the Databricks project that departs from the specification stops for the owner's approval (owner, 2026-11-21).
- The agent never contacts bankmark, the TPC or the Databricks project's author.
- Staging files produced by DIGen are never edited. The official audit, validation and visibility SQL is never edited in the repository.
